blindSummary: Nothing criminalises being trans in this country, which has a socially visible tradition of trans-feminine people; but there is no legal gender recognition, no anti-discrimination protection, no registered LGBT organisation (the one-party state restricts all civil society), and no documented recourse. Its main tourist cities are accustomed to foreign visitors, and the risk for trans visitors is administrative (an opaque state) more than violent.
blindOutOfScope: Civil-society restrictions affect all; no trans-specific mechanism documented.
blindSourceSummaries: A UN health agency's laws-and-policies database page for this country filtered to transgender-related laws and policies - an interface showing the legal instruments affecting trans people here (no criminalisation of same-sex conduct; limited specific protections).
A multilateral development bank's report on the legal status of sexual and gender minorities across this country's world region - a comparative overview covering this country among other states.

International legal-aid trust's overview of the history of LGBT criminalisation - almost 500 years of outlawing LGBT people; covering jurisdictions that criminalise and strategic litigation worldwide (this country's position: no current criminalisation but no protections).

Gay travel archive's first-person account (2000/2009): a small gay and lesbian circle in the capital - restaurants, friendships, romantic relationships; a picture of quiet, low-key gay life in this communist country.

International news network (Oct 2018): online influencers facing retribution for their posts - 'You can't post anything about the government' - the free-expression climate that also constrains LGBT visibility here.
External service of a supranational bloc: marked the International Day Against Homophobia in the capital - diplomatic visibility for LGBT rights here (page largely navigation content at fetch time).
blindLocalsOnly: No legal gender recognition and no registered LGBT organisations - resident-facing gaps.
